subject: Telemetry & consent: questions on cookies, subcontractors, and EU transfers
messages:
From: Sophie Grant <sophie.grant@acme-marketing.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on site telemetry, cookie consent, and DPA

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — the console looks promising. Before we proceed to a pilot we need to iron out a few privacy/compliance items for our security review. High-level questions below:

1) Cookies & consent: We will need to know what signals Redwood relies on for marketing telemetry (first-party cookie, third-party cookie, localStorage identifiers). Can you confirm whether the SDK sends any third-party cookies? We prefer a first-party-only approach.

2) Telemetry opt-out: Does Redwood provide a documented opt-out API or a way for us to suppress telemetry for users who decline tracking at the banner? Is there a server-side flag we can set for sessions?

3) Subprocessors & transfers: Please share the current subprocessor list and confirm whether any subprocessors process data outside the EU (we have a strict EU data residency requirement for analytics). If transfers occur, what legal mechanisms do you use (SCCs, BCRs, or customer-managed VPC options)?

4) DPA and attestations: We need a copy of your DPA and SOC2 report (or equivalent). If you have an approved DPA template we can sign, please share.

Can you put together a short response and the attachments? We have our legal and security teams on standby once we see the materials.

Thanks,
Sophie Grant
Head of Digital Analytics, Acme Marketing
Acme Corp

[Acme internal: Tom Li (tom.li@acme-marketing.com) is copied]

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on site telemetry, cookie consent, and DPA

Sophie —

Thanks for the thoughtful list. I’m looping in Laura (legal) and Kim (privacy/product) to provide the detailed artifacts. Quick answers while they pull materials:

- SDK cookies: The standard Redwood web SDK uses first-party cookies and localStorage for session KV caching and non-PII telemetry. We do not drop third-party tracking cookies by default.

- Opt-out controls: There is a server-side flag you can set at request time to disable telemetry emission. We also provide a small JS helper that reads common CMP banner states; if you prefer, we can ship a hook that integrates with your banner to automatically suppress telemetry.

- Subprocessors/transfers: I’ll attach the current subprocessor inventory and mark which locations process EU data. We support deployment to EU-only Dedicated nodes for customers requiring residency.

- DPA/SOC2: Laura will follow up with the DPA template and SOC2 report.

We’ll attach the files in the next message. Would it help if we put together a short runbook on how to integrate the opt-out flag with common CMP vendors (OneTrust, Cookiebot)?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie / Tom —

Attaching the materials you requested:
- subprocessor-list.csv (current inventory; columns: vendor, purpose, region, processing_location)
- DPA_redline_v3.docx (our standard DPA; I’ve added a few notes where customers commonly ask for clarifications)
- SOC2_report_2027.pdf (redacted report; full report available under NDA)

Summary answers to your items:
1) Cookies & telemetry: Confirmed — the SDK is first-party only. There are optional integrations that can augment identifiers (e.g., voluntary hashed email for deduplication) but these are opt-in and documented. No third-party tracker is embedded by default.

2) Telemetry opt-out: Implementation options:
   - Client-side: call Redwood.client.disableTelemetry() in page JS when consent is denied.
   - Server-side: include header X-Redwood-Telemetry: disabled on requests to the API to suppress telemetry emission and storage.
We recommend server-side enforcement for guaranteed suppression.

3) Subprocessors & EU residency: The CSV flags subprocessors that process EU data. For analytics-only telemetry we route logs to the nearest region by default; for customers requesting EU-only residency we can enable an EU-only Dedicated deployment (contracted). Transfers from EU to outside are governed by SCCs — we use standard EU SCCs for subprocessors when required. If you need customer-controlled keying/HSM or on-prem options we can scope Private deployment.

4) DPA & attestations: The attached DPA is the one we typically start from. SOC2 is included; ISO27001 is in progress. If you need the full SOC2 SOC2+ attestation we can provide that after an NDA.

Please review the DPA redline and the subprocessor CSV. If you want, we can prepare a short technical notes doc that maps the consent flows (OneTrust/Cookiebot examples) to our SDK API calls.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

A) The subprocessor CSV shows a logging provider that runs in us-east-1 — does that provider ever see raw identifiers or PII? We need assurance that PII is pseudonymized before leaving the EU.

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai

Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2027 09:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on site telemetry, cookie consent, and DPA

Tom / Sophie —

Answers inline:

A) Subprocessor data handling: The logging provider ingests anonymized event payloads by default. PII (email, phone, full name) is not written to the logging provider unless explicitly enabled by you. We pseudonymize identifiers by hashing with a customer-scoped salt prior to export. I’ve highlighted the relevant vendor rows in the CSV.

B) Opt-out header behavior: The X-Redwood-Telemetry: disabled header prevents emission to pipelines and cancels any pending KV cache flushes for that session; we treat it as authoritative for suppression at write-time. If a client toggles telemetry off mid-session, we also purge in-memory session buffers.

C) DPA & SCCs: We accept SCCs and will reference them in the DPA. For EU-only processing we can add a service-level appendix that specifies EU-only deployment (Dedicated) and routing — that is a paid/reserved option and will appear as an addendum to the DPA. We typically negotiate these as part of the Dedicated contract. Laura will propose a short clause in the next DPA version to make this explicit.

Next steps:
- Laura will incorporate the suggested clause and send DPA_redline_v4 for signature via DocuSign.
- Kim will provide a short technical runbook mapping OneTrust and Cookiebot to our client hooks.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Sophie / Tom —

I attached a short runbook (also linked in the Drive link) that shows the two integration patterns we recommend:

1) Passive: Your CMP emits an event to the page data layer; we consume the consent = false state and call Redwood.client.disableTelemetry(). Simple and minimal change.

2) Defensive: Server-side enforcement where the banner state is passed to your backend and X-Redwood-Telemetry is added to all API calls. This is our recommended option for guaranteed suppression.

Implementation notes:
- If you enable hashed_email dedup (opt-in), please ensure hashing occurs client-side with your salt; we will never accept raw emails in the telemetry payload.
- For EU residency: we can stand up an EU-only Dedicated tenancy under the same contract; this will ensure logs and aggregates remain in-region.

I’ve also included a link to the redacted SOC2 and our public subprocessor list location for ongoing updates. If you confirm you want the EU-only option, I’ll kick off an internal scoping doc and provide an order of magnitude cost/lead time.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call with your security team if they want to step through the runbook.

Cheers,
Kimberly Park
Product Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
